title: Driving Licence in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **The six months start at your Anmeldung, not at the border.** Section 29 of the Fahrerlaubnis-Verordnung gives a non-EU licence **six months** of validity from the day you register an address in Germany. The only extension is up to six more months, and only if you can make it credible that your whole stay will be under twelve months.

**An EU or EEA licence has no clock at all.** It stays valid until the date printed on it. The one trap: if you were already living in Germany when it was issued, Berlin does not have to recognise it.

**Anlage 11 FeV splits the world into three lanes, US state by US state.** **28** US jurisdictions convert with no test. **11** need the theory exam: Connecticut, DC, Florida, Indiana, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nebraska, North Carolina, Oregon, Tennessee. **13** states are not on the list at all, so those holders sit both exams from scratch, as does most of the rest of the world. All of Canada and all of Australia convert test-free.

**Berlin's fees are small: 37.50 euro** without a test, **45.10 euro** with one or from a third country, **26.50 euro** to swap an old German licence. The cost sits in the extras, and only the third-country lane needs the first aid course (about 35 to 70 euro in Berlin) and always the eyesight test.

**The desk is weeks behind, and those weeks come out of your six months.** On 15 September 2026 the Berlin licence desk was processing third-country applications filed on **31 July**, EU applications from **27 July**, Anlage 11 from **20 August** and card swaps from **27 August**.

**Old German licences expire as documents, not as entitlements.** Cards issued **2002 to 2004** must be swapped by **19 January 2027**, and the new card has to be in your hand by that date. Driving on an un-swapped one is a **10 euro** warning fine. Driving after your six months have run out is a criminal offence under section 21 StVG, worth up to a year inside.
